If found, please return to Oliver Lyonbrooke,
care of House Lyonbrooke, Baldur's Gate.
There is a reward. (A modest one.)

CHULT

a journal of the expedition

by Oliver Lyonbrooke

begun 5 Ches 1492, at sea

PRIVATE.
That means you, Luth.

Noted.
— L.

5 Ches · aboard the Brazen Pegasus

Pantarius says writing things down helps, and in the same breath that I talk too much, hence this book: now I can talk as much as I like, and nobody has to listen.

Why I'm going, in case somebody finds this on my corpse.

The Zhentarim came to Orville's wedding. Half of Baldur's Gate was there, and I am the only guest who walked out again: a sabre came down at my head and took my wings instead, and then I hid, which is the whole of the heroic story.

Pantarius tried to bring them all back. Days of ritual, more platinum than I want to think about. Nothing worked. He said it felt as if something was holding on to their souls.

Syndra Silvane says that something is in Chult, and she offers ten thousand gold to whoever ends it. I would go for free. (Don't tell her.)

The ship is the Brazen Pegasus: one mast, a handful of crew, a great deal of rope. Captain Ortimay is a rock gnome with amber goggles, a braided beard and a stingy streak just as long.

The Flaming Fist on the quay told us to buy a Charter of Exploration at Fort Beluarian: fifty gold, or exploring Chult is illegal. I hadn't known exploring could be illegal. It can, for a fee.

The company I'm keeping:

  • Undril Silvertusk: half-orc, cleric of Torm, god of rules (explains a lot). Carries a letter to Camp Righteous.
  • Salida: a guide from Chult. Three red waves tattooed on her cheek, "a gift from someone important". Does not like the Flaming Fist.
  • Ofar, from a jungle village two days out of Baldur's Gate, going to Chult to break a curse. Carries a glaive taller than me, and a shark-tiger tattoo with eleven teeth, one for every time he was reborn. ELEVEN. He gets a nosebleed every morning. He says that's the curse.
  • Luth'ayen, an elf who prays to the Raven Queen and says very little, all of it worth hearing. He stood at the stern the whole time we cast off and didn't wave once.
There was a man on the quay. Black cloak, red eyes. He was not there a moment before. I know him.

6 Ches

Salida tells stories at night. Mezro, once the greatest city in Chult, now almost empty. A hundred years ago a paladin raised an army of the dead to save it, and it was too late anyway. She also told us of a witch of red ants who haunts people, which is wonderful material to fall asleep to.

Ofar had a nightmare. Ants everywhere, and an old woman with gold coins for eyes who bit him in the throat, and all the ants bit him too, until he was red all over. She kept saying something. Then he woke up.

HER WORDS, AGAIN AND AGAIN:
KILL SOMEONE. KILL SOMEONE.

9 Ches

Fog. A whole wall of it standing on the sea, and cold, properly cold, this far south. A wind came out of it from the north, steady as a hand on your back.

And in the fog, a ship, which seemed an ordinary one until you looked at the masts and had to keep looking up, and then further up still. Nobody said anything for a long while.

Luth drew this one. Mine looked like a bathtub with ambitions.

Same day: Ofar smelled poison in the hold (paladins can do that, apparently). Under the stairs, a ratty sack full of red ants that didn't even seem to want to live, more and more of them, and at the very bottom: a ring.

Black metal, with three gold ants worked into it. Ofar kept it, and although I would very much like to take it apart, I have not asked.

10 Ches

To whoever keeps writing in my margins: I can tell you apart. One of you writes like a monk copying scripture. The other presses so hard it comes through on the next page.

11 Ches

A tiny red dragon (a PSEUDODRAGON, the size of a cat!) came out of the weather and begged for help. Its mistress had been wrecked on the rocks. Ofar stayed aboard; the rest of us took an hour's detour.

Then harpies, and a great deal of shrieking, first from above and then from us.

Her name is Xandala. Half-elf, dragon scales on her face, extremely sure of herself. She's looking for her father, Artus Cimber: human, ranger, long blond hair, an elven bow. A good fighter, travels alone. Last seen in Port Nyanzaru, heading south.

We struck a simple bargain: we help her, and she helps us.

A GREAT BOW. I MARK WELL WHO CAN FIGHT.

12 Ches

Summary of the last two days, because I am tired:

  • harpy attack
  • fish-man attack
  • fish-man attack
THE CAPTAIN HIDES SOMETHING.

13 Ches · dawn

Sails in the fog.

A black flag.

PIRATES. Twenty, thirty of them, on a ship barely bigger than ours. Our captain knew theirs. He screamed "I HATE YOU, LASKILAR!" across the water like they used to be married.

Xandala made us invisible, a fine plan until Ofar saw Undril fighting and charged in anyway. He killed one before he went down.

Luth and I went over to their ship.

Nobody saw us, so I'll write down exactly what I did, because I'm proud of it and my hands are still shaking. I crept below deck on their ship, found their gunpowder, and set off a barrel.

Their ship caught fire, and then it exploded, and most of the pirates forgot all about us and ran back across to save it. That was our moment. We fled, and I jumped from their burning rail back to ours with the whole sea lighting up behind me. I barely made it, like the hero of a proper sea shanty, though the shanties leave out the shaking.

We kept one pirate.

Afterwards, below deck. Ofar, patched up and quieter than I have ever heard him. He told me he never feels like he's enough for his tribe. I didn't have a joke for that.

THAT WAS NOT TO BE WRITTEN DOWN.

(I always have a joke.)

Salida is sick in her hammock, pale and sweating.

She is acting. She poisoned herself. My spell showed a snake beside her, and something necrotic in Ofar.

14 Ches

I asked the captain what else is waiting between us and Chult. He wouldn't say, not even when we asked less nicely, and so we have started about half a mutiny.

15 Ches

Ofar questioned our pirate. A Chultan, as expected. Salida says the serpent god Dendar made this whole island. She says it the way you say it's going to rain.

16 Ches · morning

A DRAGON TURTLE.

It nearly ate us. We gave it a lot of gold, including all of mine. There was a disagreement about that afterwards, and somehow Grig and I ended up in the sea. Ofar rowed out to fetch us, with the pirate on the second oar. Then he let the pirate go.

I have never been so poor, or so wet.

16 Ches · evening · PORT NYANZARU

A golden dragonborn landed on our deck out of the sky. Zindar, the harbourmaster. He checked our papers, which were fine; I had checked them twice.

He has a job for us, too, if we come to the guardhouse. Undril is going to the temple of Torm, and Syndra Silvane is staying with Wakanga O'tamu, so that's where we'll find her.

And Zhanthi lives here. Father's old friend. She'll know what to do with us.

The inn is called the Thundering Tiger, and it thunders.

They serve tej, which is like mead if mead wanted to fight you.

Five guide posters on the wall, every one of them promising to keep us alive in the jungle.

Xandala won't come into the jungle with us, but she'll send word whenever she hears about her father.

17 Ches

In the morning we bought light clothes at the Red Bazaar, where everything smells of dinosaur meat.

Then bells, and screaming: the guards were shutting the gate to Malar's Throat with people still on the wrong side, so we went out instead of in.

Outside, the dead, dozens of them. Undril fought beside us; we put some down, got people into a temple, and sat there afterwards for a long time.

MANY. I CEASED TO COUNT AND FOUGHT ON.

The priest there, Parlas, says the attacks are getting worse, and that the dead are "the fallen from last time". He gave us an amulet, and a favour owed by the high priest of Savras.

later · Zhanthi's villa

She had our laundry washed and let me have a bath, which after twelve days at sea was a religious experience.

And then she told me something, and I want to write it slowly.

Her miners found me. As a baby. In Finger's Gold.

In CHULT.

Father never told me where I came from. Whenever I asked, he went quiet. I'm not angry. Not much. A bit.

Also from Zhanthi: the merchant princes have ruled for nine years. The Flaming Fist only bother with the jungle. Her son is a guide at Fort Beluarian. Most of the city guard are Zhentarim. Wonderful.

Syndra Silvane, at Wakanga O'tamu's (prince of magical knick-knacks).

Old, very polite, and coughing blood into her handkerchiefs. She was raised from the dead decades ago, so the curse is eating her now.

It comes from an artifact called the Soulmonger, somewhere deep in the jungle. She knows this from a LICH, with whom she has some kind of deal, and about which she will say nothing more.

Where to start, she says: Mezro, or the oracle in the west, or Camp Righteous, or the witch of Mbala. Four doors into the jungle, and nobody knows which one opens onto the Soulmonger.

Syndra would not name the lich. Ask again. — L.

Back at the Tiger we read the guide posters properly. Five guides, and the best poster is Salida's, because it is mostly about the other four: charlatans, all of them, and old Hew has blue mist fever.

So I went out and asked what blue mist fever is: you faint, and then you see things. I have made a note to myself not to catch it.

Before we leave: tell Syndra. She gives us rations, thirty days each.

In the evening I went down to the dinosaur pens and rented a racing dinosaur for tomorrow's race, although I have never ridden a dinosaur in my life. How hard can it be?

Five gold.

I intend to win it back, with interest.

18 Ches · THE RACE

Six of us at the start. Quilgoch, a tortle, on something long-legged. Faroul and Gondolo on their own triceratops. Tiryk on Banana Candy. Kenkakil on Juicy Steaks, who is a stegosaurus. Dark, a gnome, on an allosaurus, which seemed unfair to everybody else's dinosaur.

And me, on five gold's worth of painted triceratops.

THE RACE WAS OLLI'S.
100 GOLD.

We hired a guide: Musharib, the albino dwarf, one of very few dwarves in Chult. One day he wants his clan's old forge back. Until then, he'll settle for our gold.

Zindar's job: a notice, sealed with an eye. A thousand gold for whoever finds the hideout of the pirates Laskilar (hello again), Elok Jaharwon and Zaroum al-Saryak.

The players never followed this job. This would have been an opportunity for Luth to discover more of his backstory, to raid the pirate enclave and to get a ship to skip large sections of the jungle trek.
Elok and Laskilar work with the fish-men. Zaroum was a merchant prince once. Likes gemstones.

Ofar went to the temple and asked Savras four questions. He told me what he saw, and I drew it as well as I could from that:

He asked how to lift his curse, and saw a misty mountain plateau with ruined huts, one still whole, and beside it a young Chultan with wings. An angel(?!) He asked where Pu'pu is, and saw the same place again.

He asked for the pirates' hideout: a sea cave with a big ship inside, houses, the sea flowing in. And last he asked for the Soulmonger, and saw a city in the jungle under fog, snakes on the ground, something dark. A jungle that didn't look like Chult.

19 Ches

We leave. Upriver by boat: Ofar, Luth, me, Undril and Musharib, and Port Nyanzaru getting smaller behind us until it was only a smell, and then not even that.

20 Ches

Ryath roots: knobbly, ugly, and good food. And wukka nuts: shake one and the shell GLOWS. A lamp that needs no oil! Luth says that is all they are good for. I have three in my waistcoat and plans for all of them.

One is wedged in the oarlock right now, and I'm writing by its light. The jungle doesn't sleep at all; it just changes which animals are doing the shouting.

21 Ches

A canoe came drifting towards us, and in it lay a dead elf, killed by goblin arrows. A diary and a locket with a picture of an elf woman: Nara. He and his brother had only reached Chult on the fifteenth, barely prepared, on the way to Camp Righteous. The last entry was from yesterday.

We gave him a fire burial.

Night. I keep thinking of them: two brothers in one boat, with no plan and hardly any supplies. That could have been us, and some days it still is.

22 Ches

ARROW!

22 Ches · later

The arrow was goblins. Then came more arrows and more goblins, and all that noise brought the dead out of the jungle as well. Somewhere in the middle of it I fell over. I only know how it ended because I woke up afterwards and everyone else was still standing.

Ofar found a plant he knows from home: drumbassar, a leaf you chew. It keeps you going.

Blue mist on the river, rising off a tall blue plant two metres high, and it gets into your head, so you must not breathe it. I held my breath as long as an owl can. Which is long.IT ISN'T.

Musharib knew a safer place to sleep, a shrine of Ubtao, four metres by four, with a fire bowl on the altar that never goes out and, carved on the wall, one very large figure standing over many small houses.

That night Ofar had the dream again, the ants and the old woman, but this time someone pulled him out at the last moment: Pu'pu, the witch his shaman sent him to find. When he woke up, he wrote this into my book himself:

MY OATH. WIDOW GROAT, THE RED ANT WITCH, HATH PUT HER CURSE IN MY BLOOD. I SHALL FIND HER, AND BY MY HAND SHE SHALL DIE. THIS I SWEAR ON MINE ELEVEN TEETH. SHOULD IT COST ME A TWELFTH, I SHALL PAY IT.
IN INK, THAT IT STAND.

Then we talked until it got light. My own oath is smaller, and it has a box to tick:

☐ FIND THE RED ANT WITCH

23 Ches

Ofar got up this morning stronger than he lay down. I think the oath did it; even the way he stands has changed.

Food report.

We boil all our water now.

A kayak came downriver with three locals in it. They had taken "something" back from the Batiri goblins and would not say what. Weirdos, in my professional opinion.

Batiri in the trees. They wear huge painted wooden masks, and when they want to reach you they climb on each other's shoulders. I am not making this up.

24 Ches

Then crocodiles, many of them, and one that was less a crocodile than a boat with teeth.

At night a dinosaur walked through the camp, so we moved the camp.

Ofar wanted to paint this one himself. He borrowed my brushes. I'm getting them back eventually.

25 Ches · Camp Righteous

We found it empty and wrecked, with dead zombies everywhere and claw marks on everything. Their log says: ghoul attack, the wounded sent two days upriver to Camp Vengeance, better manned.

Then the statue: a stone man with a crocodile on his back, tall as a tower, a door at his feet. Inside: a trapdoor, swinging axes, a door with a riddle, and a spiral staircase that BITES.

For science:

Upstairs, paintings on the walls. I copied two:

A hero with a glaive killing a T-rex. An army of the dead. Beasts. And a man who is a snake from the waist down, leading the dead, killing the hero. A city sinking deeper into the jungle.

I MARK WHERE EACH PICTURE TOOK PLACE.
A PICTURE WITHOUT A PLACE IS OF NO USE.
Six pictures, not four. The hero has a name: Na'Nbuzo? — L.

On a pedestal, a heavy clay jug. I said "Krabash", old Chultan for water, and it filled up.

LUTH SPOKE THOSE WORDS. NOT OLLI.

We ran. A blade caught me on the way out and I went down. Somebody patched me up. (Thank you, somebody.) Then we came out into the light and saw them:

Goblins on our boat, stealing our BOAT.

25 Ches · still

We got the boat back, and the cargo with it, though in all the excitement I nearly fell into the trapdoor again and then put a hole in our own boat.

We plugged the hole with a dead goblin, who fits it perfectly. I am not proud of that, or only a little.

All the noise brought a few of the dead out of the trees. We put them down again.

YESTERDAY A BLADE FELLED OLLI. TODAY HE PUT A HOLE IN OUR BOAT. HE IS WELL.

25 Ches · evening

The jug came with us. It answers to Old Chultan. Say krabásh and it pours water. Say bassúr and it pours wine. Say najj and it pours honey, slowly, while everybody watches. Luth carries it. He said the word first; I have been corrected.

Since then I collect Old Chultan words wherever I can get them, jug or no jug. Kaun is warm, bzzu is a bee, dalar is red. There is one more, which Ofar thought was hilarious. It is not a jug word, and I'm not writing it down.

WATER, WINE, HONEY. WE BEAR IT FOR THE WATER.

26 Ches

Three stakes by the river. Two skeletons, and between them an elf, smeared with honey, and the bees were eating him. A goblin mask hung over them as a warning to people like us.

I keep wondering whether he was the brother the diary in the canoe talked about.

Luth went to him alone, and when he came back he said only one word: dead.

LUTH SAYS THE ELF WAS DEAD. HE LIES. I SAY NOTHING. NOT YET.

Later a boat of the Order of the Gauntlet came downriver: armoured men, and wounded ones, on their way to Port Nyanzaru. Ofar laid his hands on one of them who was dying, and then he wasn't any more. We took that one back upriver with us.

JOSHUA. I SAVED HIM WITH THESE HANDS. FOR THAT WERE THEY MADE.

26 Ches · evening · CAMP VENGEANCE

We had to wait outside before they let us in, among bones piled against the wall and mud everywhere, and the smell: Camp Vengeance stinks of death and dung.

Sergeant Harlan Mott says the attacks on the camps are organised. Someone is leading the dead. Our guesses, in order of popularity: a curse, a necromancer, red wizards.

Mott suspects a leader. And a friend of — (the ink ran). — L.

Commander Sir Niles Breakbone has a short fuse, thirty fighters and fifty living souls in his camp. We brought him a message from Sir Ironheart: no more soldiers for three months, and a box of healing potions instead.

HE LOSES HIS TEMPER AND INSULTS ALL. A COMMANDER WHO SHOUTS HAS LOST ALREADY.

His lieutenant is a dwarf, Ord Firebeard. The day after tomorrow Ord takes an expedition south into the swamp, where red wizards have been seen. We're going with him.

There is a gunsmith in this camp: Turon. He's from the jungle, speaks a little Common and a lot of hands, and he builds pistols. A border-crosser, he calls himself. A pistoleer. The others think he's a bit strange, and they're right, but we only talked for a short while and I made it count.

He told me something I have underlined three times in my head:

A Lantanese airship crashed into the jungle south of the swamp.

A Lantanese airship, crashed, and carrying guns: Lantanese guns, and if Turon is right, one of them is the kind of weapon they tell legends about. Nobody has picked it up yet.

The healer, Mirila, gave us a lecture on what kills you here. Blue mist fever takes days to weeks, and only magic helps. Shivering sickness comes from insects, and the Chultans swear by a red, star-shaped fruit from tall trees in the swamp. And throat leeches: drink unboiled water and they suck onto the inside of your mouth. I have never been so glad we boil ours.

ASK MIRILA OF THE OTHER SICKNESSES. HERE IT IS THE SMALL THINGS THAT KILL.

26 Ches · night

Then the cold came, breath-steaming cold in the middle of the jungle; fog rolled over the palisade, and out of the fog came ghosts.

They went for Breakbone, and Breakbone ran, while we stayed and fought them off, which is more than can be said for some people.

Then I did something petty: while everyone was busy, I poured red wine into Breakbone's bed.

27 Ches

We told everyone who would listen what a coward he is and how wonderful Ord is. Luth even tried to convince Ord he'd make the better commander. The expedition left a day early.

On the riverbank, an army of skeletons, standing in ranks, perfectly still, little red lights in their eyes. In front of them a heap of bodies, dragged one by one to a star scratched into the ground.

Luth went over to look and came back carrying a staff, and then the skeletons moved, and we paddled.

Further down, the river was frozen. Forty metres of solid ice in the middle of the jungle, icicles on the lianas, and so cold my feathers stood up on their own. Somebody had walked across before us: footprints in shoes, a day or two old. Two people.

Minus-something degrees in the jungle doesn't just happen. Somebody did this.

28 Ches

Nothing came of it. Then the swamp began, wide and wet, with hardly a tree in it.

29 Ches

First came a cloud of stinking mosquitoes, and after them ten more the size of small dogs.

One of them came straight at my face. I had my pistol in my hand and hadn't even lifted it. Then Ofar's glaive went through it a hand's width from my beak. He saved my life and didn't even look round.

One of Ord's soldiers was stung and went grey and feverish; Ofar cured him. Ord killed loads of them himself; he is so great that I want to have his child.

10 deathsquitos. — L.

30 Ches · dawn

Ofar woke me early and showed me something in the mud outside the camp: half a pentagram. And footprints, leading back into the camp.

We told everyone. Nobody said a name, though I think everybody thought one.

LUTH? A TRAITOR? A THIEF? I SHALL WATCH HIM.

And then, a little later, this:

A lump of earth fifty metres on a side, hanging a hundred metres above the swamp and drifting a little in the wind, with one dead tree on top and roots hanging down from it like veins.

I have no idea how, and I would very much like to.

The Heart of Ubtao. 50 × 50 × 50 m. A stump. — L.

30 Ches · Lake Erdolon

Drizzle, and good visibility for once. The river narrows and runs into a lake.

The legend goes that the aldani lived here, until Ubtao turned them into lobster people for overfishing the river. I have so many questions about this.

UBTAO DOES NOT JEST. NO FISHING ON THIS RIVER. SO BE IT.

Looking for a place to camp, I (!!!) found a little jetty in the reeds.

Luth and I followed the planks to a small pond, where we found a fishing rod and a bucket but nobody to use them, and a smell like a hundred dead things.

It was the pond. Or something living in it: a heap of rotting plants that stood up and came for us, with things tangled in it I won't describe. We call it the Shambilimomba.

We won, and nobody even got hurt. Ofar painted it afterwards and spelled it wrong.

On another island stood a hut on stilts, and in it lived an aldani. A real one. His name is Kruuk, he has claws and eyes on stalks, and he told us the island is safe. We fetched the boat and slept there. (Luth "meditated". Elves don't sleep, apparently. They sit very still with their eyes shut and insist it isn't the same thing.)

An old people. Long unseen. — L.

30 Ches · night

In the night somebody carved a pentagram into Kruuk's door.

In the morning we looked at Kruuk very hard in the daylight, and he was still a lobster, and still friendly.

I know who I think did it, and I'm not writing it down.

A PENTAGRAM AGAIN. SOMEONE HERE TRIFLES WITH THE DEAD.

1 Tarsakh

East shore of the lake, two days of food, walking towards the Heart. Ord's soldiers came along, including one I've been calling Torsten. Torsten talks a lot, and the more he talks, the more suspicious he seems.

A scrap of red cloth, a week old. Red wizards? Then a camp: the fire pit buried under moss, two trees cut down nearby, and no tracks leading away. In the ashes, burnt paper with words in a language none of us knows. Ofar found a skull carved out of wood, the size of a plum.

ONE RED WIZARD TO THE SOUTH-EAST. THEN TWO OR THREE FOLK TO THE SOUTH. WE FOLLOW.

1 Tarsakh · night

Torsten and I caught Luth drawing a pentagram in the ground with that staff. I scuffed it out. He came at us, and skeletons climbed out of the star. I fired and didn't hit, and nothing anyone else tried hit him either.

Ofar took the staff out of his hands and kicked it into the swamp, and then Luth was Luth again.

I prayed for forgiveness until morning. — L.
I KICKED THE STAFF INTO THE SWAMP. AT DAWN I LOOKED. THERE IT LAY STILL.

2 Tarsakh · the Heart

Someone lives on the Heart for now: Valindra Shadowmantle, an elf and a wizard, very elegant and a little arrogant. She opened a portal for us and we stepped through, up into a room inside the rock.

Valindra told us more than anyone has since we landed. The Soulmonger belongs to a lich called Acererak. It traps the souls of the dead, and it is the reason for the curse. It is probably in Omu, an old city in the jungle, guarded by yuan-ti.

The red wizards want a ring that belongs to Artus Cimber, Xandala's father, and the ring makes ice. (The river!)

And two more places for the list: Nangalore, an old temple on the River Olung where you can ask a goddess for answers, and Firefinger, a huge pillar of rock in the jungle, full of flying creatures.

Other owlins in Chult???

FIREFINGER. OWLINS DWELL THERE ALSO. OLLI WILL WISH TO GO.

3 Tarsakh

Back to the boat and back down the river. A boat came the other way, full of fresh adventurers, and in it sat Salida. What a — no. I'm a gentleman. What a woman.

That night Luth put down some skeletons on his own. I didn't ask where they came from.

4 Tarsakh

We said goodbye to Ord and went north-west through the jungle until, in the evening, cliffs rose ahead of us and a canyon pointed the way to Mbala.

5 Tarsakh

There were pterosaurs in the canyon; we lured them down to us and dealt with them, and I notice we are getting better at this.

In the evening we found an old hut with half a roof, patched it with our tents and slept dry for once.

6 Tarsakh · MBALA

Mbala sits on top of a plateau, and the only way up is round the north side: a dry riverbed with steps hacked into the stone, properly awful ones, with skulls on them.

Ofar fell, and the vines caught him, and somewhere below us the pterosaurs screamed the whole time.

I FELL. A VINE CAUGHT ME. I CLIMBED ON.

On top we found a dead village, a fortress to the west and a light to the east. We went towards the light, and out of the house came a VERY old woman.

The witch of Mbala.

Pu'pu, the one Ofar's shaman sent him to find, who has quite certainly murdered everyone in the village and keeps looking at me as if I were dinner.

She told us the oracle is to the west, in a ziggurat called Orolunga. And that near Omu we'll need a black orchid from the gardens of Nangalore, or her sisters will get into our heads.

Her sisters.

Three of them are in Omu, and together with the lich they made the Soulmonger: Widow Groat, coins on her eyes and red ants (the old woman from Ofar's nightmares, and now we know where she lives); Baggy Nanna, who hides in a leather bag; and Peggy Deadbells, bloated and steaming, who looks like something you'd find at the bottom of a well.

And there is one more sister, Zuzuwika, who is the shaman of Ofar's own tribe.

I drank her tea, which was very bitter, and then everything in me cramped at once. She shut the door. Musharib smashed it open again, I sprinted out into the daylight, and then I was lying on the ground looking at the sky.

OLLI DRANK OF HER TEA. NOT I.
ZUZUWIKA!
OUR SHAMAN. SHE SENT ME TO PU'PU.
AND SHE IS THEIR SISTER?
FIVE SISTERS. ONE IN MY DREAMS. ONE IN MY VILLAGE.
I SHALL ASK HER AT HOME, TO HER FACE.

6 Tarsakh · night

I woke up in an empty house in the village and heard monkeys. Flying monkeys. We fed them a little, and one, braver than the rest, came right up to me while the others hung back.

ONE MONTH OR TWO, ERE THE CURSE KILLS ME.
THE OTHERS NEED NOT KNOW.

7 Tarsakh

We looked through the fortress in the west and found a few useful things. Then down the cliff again, and Ofar fell again.

TWO CLIFFS. TWICE NEARLY DEAD. ELEVEN TEETH ARE ENOUGH.

Ofar wrote something in my margin last night. I have read it, and I am not going to say anything about it yet.

8 Tarsakh

Then west, towards the oracle, and on the way we were attacked by a bush: a walking bush in the shape of a person. I want that on record.

9 Tarsakh

In the night Luth's eyes bled, and in the morning he wanted to go to Camp Vengeance at once, that very hour.

1. Undead T-rex, a rider in a red robe, a palisade: Vengeance. 2. Someone before a skeleton army: known. 3. Ravens.

We left our packs at the camp and went to Orolunga anyway.

The ziggurat tests you on the way up. Thorns that open if you hold up an orange-and-purple flower. A stair that crumbles under you unless you carry a red feather. And a stair full of snakes, where you slither and hiss your way up, as all of us did, with varying dignity.

All the way up, tiny spirits watched us from the leaves, none bigger than my hand, each behind a carved wooden mask with a crown of leaves. Musharib called them chwingas. I would swear one of them laughed when Ofar hissed.

Voices from inside: Common, with a hiss. Ofar checked for traps and declared all clear, bravely, since he doesn't even have darkvision.

HOLD UP THE RIGHT THING AND THE WAY OPENS. IT IS SIMPLE.

Then a great stone gate that you can't see through. We all stepped through it together. Musharib and I were still holding up our flower and our feather; the others weren't. On the other side I could only see Musharib.

(The others ended up in a copy of the room, they told us later. Same cushions, same smoke, no oracle. A whole fake room, just for people who don't listen.)

AN EMPTY ROOM. WE WAITED. NAUGHT CAME.
NEXT TIME, I HOLD THE FEATHER.

A bright room, incense, cushions. A man, a dinosaur-person, and the oracle: a snake five metres long, black scales, red belly.

The snake answered our questions, slowly, as if every answer cost it something. "There is nothing left in Mezro. Seek paradise, not Mezro." Omu lies between the Peaks of Flame and the Valley of Lost Honour, guarded by Ras Nsi, a paladin who damned the jungle, and his followers will soon attack Camp Vengeance.

The pirates' camp is west of the Aldani Basin. And Hrakhamar holds a hundred fire newts, a thousand undead, one dragon and four times the treasure. Hrakhamar is the forge Musharib wants back. Good luck, Musharib.

The man was Artus Cimber, and the dinosaur is called Dragonbait. Artus has no idea who Xandala is.

Xandala is not his daughter.

Your oracle: Mezro. Paradise, gardens, waterfalls. — L.

We pushed through the night, back to our camp.

10 Tarsakh

We slept until the afternoon, built the camp up properly, and slept again while Ofar went hunting.

11 Tarsakh

Walking back to the boat, we heard a humming from the west and were too slow to run: undead mosquitoes.

Both my pistols misfired.

Both of them. I was stung, and Ofar fixed me.

TOO SLOW TO FLEE. SO WE FOUGHT.

12 Tarsakh

Luth is missing a tuft of hair. Musharib says a monkey demon took it.

The next night Ofar heard it coming and threw a javelin. It came back covered in black blood, and the blood is eating the iron.

MY JAVELIN CAME BACK BLACK. THE BLOOD EATS IRON. I WOULD HAVE MY JAVELIN BACK.

13 Tarsakh

The boat was where we had left it, though a quarter of the food had gone elsewhere. We stacked the crates so one of us can always sleep and we never have to stop: a houseboat, more or less.

14 Tarsakh

Rain. The boat filled up slowly, so I built a hose out of a liana and sucked the water out over the side. We carried the boat round the ice and kept going.

OLLI MAKES A PUMP OF A LIANA. THE BOAT FLOATS. I COMPLAIN NO MORE.

We reached Camp Vengeance late in the evening. Ord said there had been attack after attack, and we got ready.

Then they came: dead men, and dead dinosaurs.

14 Tarsakh · the same night

The gate went down, and everyone ran to it.

Breakbone ran the other way, and a dead triceratops caught him on its horn almost at once. Very sad.

Apart from him hardly anyone died, and we held.

BREAKBONE IS DEAD. ON HIM, AN AMULET OF NECROMANCY. THAT I SHALL REMEMBER.

I went through Breakbone's things. Around his neck: a talisman that looks exactly like Luth's staff. Ofar has it now, wrapped in a blanket; we had it looked at, and it is necromancy.

15 Tarsakh

We slept, then went out with the others to find whoever leads the dead. Ofar followed the tracks of something enormous to a hill with a circle of standing stones: a ritual site, for raising the dead in great numbers and mending them.

We tried to sneak up on it, and then Luth shouted.

A dead tyrannosaurus, and on its back a rider in a robe with a dead face, exactly as in Luth's vision. Luth turned them both back with the light of the Raven Queen, and still we were thoroughly beaten up, and only just won.

Henry fell.

THE RITUAL MENDS THE DEAD. A STRONG NECROMANCY. HENRY HAS FALLEN.

We carried him back to the camp.

Ord gave a speech to the twenty-odd who are left. Ofar started chanting his name, and then all of us did.

Ord won't leave this place. I think it's the only home he has left.

ORD! ORD! ORD!

15 Tarsakh · morning

We buried Henry.

Then Ord asked one more thing of us: would we take his wounded to Port Nyanzaru? Nine of them. Two with throat leeches, two who are dying, five who'll live. And a letter for the priest Parlas at the temple of Torm. (Very important.)

Our escort: Undril, who sailed with us from Baldur's Gate; Vinslev, a local, who leads; Rhobar, big and silent; and Emmanuel.

Nine wounded and a jungle full of things that eat people. What could possibly go wrong.

On the way out we checked the place where the skeleton army had stood, and of course it was the same ritual circle.

15 Tarsakh · night · Camp Righteous

We pushed hard and made Camp Righteous. I kept watch with Emmanuel until four in the morning. Ofar had his nightmare again.

And then, out of nowhere, there was a triceratops in our camp, sniffing at him.

He says the witch gave her to him in the dream. She is his steed now: a paladin can call one with a prayer, and Ofar's comes as a triceratops. Her name is Scarlett.

IN A DREAM, PU'PU GRANTED ME A STEED.
A TRICERATOPS. SCARLETT IS HER NAME.
WHEN I CALL, SHE COMES.

16 Tarsakh

Ofar healed one of the dying men and one of the sick. Then Luth cast a spell on Scarlett so she could walk on water.

And now she pulls the damn boats along at sixty feet, all four of them, twice as fast as we could row.

An hour later, a dead man on the bank, thrown against a tree, his back broken but not a scratch on him; thirteen gold and a sabre, and around him giant footprints, and a wolf's.

Two hours after that, the giants themselves, in white, with a wolf the size of a horse. They asked us about a man called Artus Cimber. Then everything happened very fast.

WE STRUCK FIRST.
ONE BOAT WE LOST, AND ONE MAN.

16 Tarsakh · afternoon

We lost the last boat, and Rupert, one of the wounded. He was Emmanuel's friend. We buried him where the giants couldn't reach. Before that I gave Ofar my amulet of protection. He needs it more than I do.

Later: a wounded stegosaurus crashing across the river, and behind it four towers of goblins, sixteen in all, shouting at us to stop. Luth shouted something back. They attacked. I got hit and fell overboard, and the incredibly manly Rhobar pulled me back into the boat.

Another boat came upriver: five adventurers on their way to the oracle for the priests of Savras. They didn't look well prepared. (I know. I know.)

In the evening we camped at the place with the underground bunker. Chultans had a fire going and let us share it. They're on their way to Mbala to kill the witch, because she ate their village. We neither stopped them nor helped them.

Night. I couldn't sleep, so I'm writing. Something is moving in the river, and I'm sure it's just a fish, a big fish, and now they're climbing out: two and a half metres tall, dead, and covered in mushr

About the page before this one: I didn't put the book down in time. Most of that isn't ink. I've decided it isn't mine, and I've decided not to find out whose it is. If you're reading this: don't lick your finger to turn that page.

Luth drew what came out of the river the next morning, from memory, and he got it right. We won, but afterwards half of us were going fungal, me included: Rotting Pox. It itches.

What helps: a blue flower from the swamp called Moonglow or, not as well, a yellow jungle weed. Or magic. In the end everyone was cured.

One of the wounded didn't live through the night.

Rotting pox. Cure: no idea, needs longer study. Magic helps, so: the paladin. — L.

17 Tarsakh

At sea: two plesiosaurs. We steered straight at them, and they fled.

STEER STRAIGHT AT THEM, AND THEY FLEE.

Port Nyanzaru by night. We carried the wounded up to the temple of Torm one by one and gave Parlas the letter. He thanked us with two strong healing potions and a potion of feather fall, and told us about a man called Islav, who lives alone half a day up the Tiryki at a little pier. Bring potion ingredients, he said.

We slept in the temple. My skin still itches.

18 Tarsakh · Port Nyanzaru

Morning. We hadn't even reached the market when I saw a face I know, nailed to a wall.

WANTED.
Luth'ayen.
500 gold.
Alive only.

Report to Ifan Talro'a, merchant prince.

It's a good likeness, better than anything I could have drawn of him.

Luth looked at it for a long time. Then he said, "Meet back here in an hour?" and was gone into the crowd.

LUTH IS WANTED, FOR GOLD. NOT FOR THEFT. FOR SOMETHING WORSE?

Ofar and I spent the hour on important business. There is a dinosaur covered in spikes walking round the market with a bagel stall on its back. It sells bamboo bagels.

Then a craftsman for Scarlett: Alequinn, a gnome with a beard down to his belt and spectacles like two portholes. He'll build her a howdah, a little house for her back. He asked a hundred gold, and we talked him down to seventy-five.

Somehow it all comes to a hundred and forty-one gold and six silver; we paid seventy, and the rest is due when the work is done.

WE AGREED ON 75. HE WROTE 141 AND 6. GNOMES.

When we found Luth again, he had seen three shady men in the crowd, looking for him. Someone is hunting him, and the same name keeps coming up: Ifan Talro'a, merchant prince.

WHO HUNTS LUTH HUNTS US. NONE HUNTS US.

So Ofar and I went to ask Zhanthi, and on the way we took a long look at Ifan's villa.

Two storeys, elegant, a lot of windows, and a spiked fence two metres high all the way round. The side with the stairs isn't guarded so well. On the other side: a ladder, trees, bushes in the garden.

Zhanthi didn't know much about Luth's trouble. About Ifan, she knew this:

He trusts nobody, and he has no family. The flying snakes that carry messages round the city are his. He isn't dangerous himself, but he has friends in the city watch, which here means the Zhentarim. His office is on the second floor, north side.

And then she told me one more thing about him.

He has something to do with the death of my parents.

I have written that line three times now. It doesn't get any shorter.

Orville's wedding, the sabre, everyone I grew up with: and a merchant prince on the other side of the sea, a man who has never once met me, had a hand in it.

18 Tarsakh · the temple of Savras

The priests of Savras told us about Nangalore. It's a temple garden, built to honour a queen called Zalkoré: orchids everywhere, water running down over the terraces, very old, and very well kept. It used to be called Kanandje. The queen still lives there, they say, only changed, and maybe not alone. People who go there don't come back.

NEVER INSULT ZALKORÉ. FOR NO CAUSE WHATEVER.

Then they showed us a vision.

Twenty knights in black and yellow under a banner, getting ready. Then the same knights on three small boats, with wounded. The Company of the Yellow Banner, a few months ago.

Then Port Castigliar, abandoned and full of the dead, and after it Mezro, which looked no better.

Ofar's list for the day had one line on it for me: Oli: buy a weapon. So I went to look.

A musket: a hundred and fifty gold. A blunderbuss: a hundred and twenty. A plain revolver, six shots: a hundred. And a magnum revolver in brass and steel: two hundred and fifty. TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY.

I looked at it for a long time.

We also hired a guide: Azaka Stormfang, who wants her mask back from the pterafolk on Firefinger. That's where we're going next. She'll wait for us at the harbour at one in the morning on the 21st.

PARLAS SAYS AZAKA AND EKU KNOW THE EAST. AZAKA WE HIRED.

The plan: get into Ifan's house at night. In the evening we went back up to the princes' ward to look around. I chatted with the guards as smoothly as any bard, and looked around about as well as a blind mole.

19 Tarsakh

Shopping: make-up, and food for ten days. Thieves' tools: nobody would sell us any, not even Musharib's friend the smith. So we went to the black market at Tiryki Anchorage.

I counted my money very, very obviously, and a young thief took the bait. Then he took us to his boss.

The boss did not care for our way of asking.

I put five bullets into him.

WE STRUCK HIM SENSELESS.

We took his thieves' tools and a gun and ran. Somebody shot at us on the way out, and a thug stepped into the alley in front of us and said:

"Ortimay sends his regards."

Ortimay. Our captain Ortimay, from the Brazen Pegasus. What did we ever do to him? (Apart from the half mutiny.)

WE SLEW ONE AND LEFT THE ANCHORAGE BLOCK. SWIFTLY.

Now I'm back at the temple of Torm, and my pistols are still warm while I write this.

20 Tarsakh

At the temple we helped heal a few more people. Then we spent the day searching the whole city for anything that makes you invisible, found nothing at all, and went to look at the spot where we'll land tonight.

And we picked up Scarlett's howdah.

IT BECOMES SCARLETT WELL. SHE KNOWS IT.

Hammocks built in. With a lever. And a rope ladder. Alequinn is a genius. We still owe him seventy-one gold and six silver, and I'm writing that down so I can't pretend I forgot.

20 Tarsakh · afternoon, in the howdah

I'm writing this lying in one of the new hammocks. Half my face is black. (Make-up. For the dark.)

Tonight is Operation Plum Jam. I don't remember who named it. It might have been me.

  • south to the water;
  • Scarlett walks us across to the pier under the temple of Sune;
  • over the bridge, over the wall;
  • into Ifan's house. Office: second floor, north side.

20 Tarsakh · night

We set off in the evening and it took FOREVER to get there.

On the way Scarlett walked into a fence, by accident and very loudly.

Around midnight we reached the pier, crossed the bridge and climbed the wall on the rope. A Silence, and a guard went down inside it: Zhentarim. I unalived him.

Up onto the porch roof with the rope, another Silence, and in through the window.

Ifan's office. A book by the Harpers about the Zhentarim: the Harpers had a mole among them. And under the desk, a heavy package in oilcloth that smelled of sulphur. We took it. Nobody wanted to be the one to open it.

And a letter. I've copied it here word for word, because I want it in my own hand.

"Ifan, the wedding went the way we'd discussed. Nobody gives a damn about the Lyonbrockes any more. Their crates full of guns are ours now, enough to stir up Baldur's Gate properly. As for Zhanthi, she can look after herself. Without her dear arms dealers she'll hardly be better off. Maybe her trade collapses, maybe not. Suits us either way. See what you make of it. If there's more to do, you know where to find us.
— For the Network"

Lyonbrooke.

It's LYONBROOKE. They killed everyone at my brother's wedding, and they can't even spell us.

Orville's wedding, my family, their guns, Zhanthi's trade: to these people it was all one piece of business. "The wedding went the way we'd discussed." Ifan was in on it.

For a while I said nothing, and neither did Luth, because he had found something too.

A picture of Luth, and under it a name I had never heard: Elandor Sylrien Thulnarië.

And a contract: seven hundred and fifty gold for handing him over, "in no way harmed, for such an offence would damage the ritual." Signed in red by Ifan Talro'a, and by somebody called Nithra'xil, whose signature has little drawings round it that I didn't like looking at.

The poster in the market had said five hundred, so somebody was planning to keep the difference.

In Ifan's house, a picture: Elandor Sylrien Thulnarië. A holy task, handed down by the parents. A holy oath. 750 gp. Not to be harmed. Ritual of — Ifan, Nithra'xil. Thulnarië: a high family in Thulthanthar.

After midnight we got to his bedroom door. I picked the lock. The lock bit first: some spell, and every feather I own stood on end.

Then a guard came round the corner and saw us.

21 Tarsakh · after midnight

Luth told the guard to come closer, in that voice you obey, and he came. I took him down all on my own with my blowgun. I am very proud of the blowgun.

Then Ifan himself. We pulled him out of his bed, I got a lasso round his foot, and we dragged him into the Silence and gagged him; once he was quiet, Luth let the Silence go and read his thoughts while we asked our questions.

He finally gave me a name.

KARALA STOLA.

Baldur's Gate.

Sure of himself in questioning, because he knows. We were lied to. An island in the city, here. They came to Chult with a lot of money. They come when we want. — L.

After that we were finished with Ifan Talro'a. I'm not going to write about that part.

THEN WE SLEW HIM.

More guards came, so we went out of the window into the neighbour's garden, Luth fighting his way through while Ofar and I ran for the wall.

The wall is two metres of spikes, and I am not two metres of anything. So Ofar threw me. Twice I came back down on the wrong side of it; the third time I flew up and over, and in the same breath Ofar stepped through the air: a puff of silver mist, gone from the garden, there on top of the wall, just in time to catch me before I went down the other side.

THE THIRD THROW. THE FIRST TWO COUNT NOT.

Over the wall we went, over the bridge and back to Scarlett, with a few more guards on the way, and then we were walking across the harbour on top of the water while every bell in the city rang behind us.

21 Tarsakh · two in the morning

We landed near the piers and I went to find Azaka. She was frightened. I tried to talk her round and failed, and then Luth tried in his own way, which is the frightening way, and after that she stayed behind.

OLLI TOLD HER IT WAS OUR DOING. HE CANNOT LIE. AT TIMES THAT IS A BURDEN.

Then south, up the Tiryki. We teleported past the first waterfall and hacked our way through the jungle round the second, and when we finally rested, Ofar snored while Luth did his elf thing, sitting up all night with his eyes closed.

I have added one line to my list of things to do:

Karala Stola, in Baldur's Gate.

Supposedly, that is the one responsible for the attack on my family, and one day I am going to knock on that door.

THE FIRST WATERFALL: ONE TELEPORT, AND IT LAY BEHIND US.

21 Tarsakh · afternoon

Riding on, we stopped on the riverbank to gather plants.

Something called drombalar that keeps you awake. I'm not sure that's what it's called.

Glitter violets: 8 hand-sized flowers make 1–2 potions. — L.

Then a boy burst out of the jungle and jumped into the river, three deinonychus right behind him. We went for them; two died, and the third ran.

The boy didn't say a word. Luth said something ugly about the boy's people, and I gave Luth a name for that which I'm not going to write down.

That evening we found a pier under the water, and the boy led us through the trees to a treehouse. That's where Islav lives, the mad potion-brewer Parlas told us about.

He gave me a potion and I drank it on the spot. Then he told me what it was: a potion of flying.

Ofar got one too, and didn't drink it. He's sceptical.

Islav says the boy is called Teemo. At least, Islav thinks so. He was meant to be sacrificed to Ubtao, and he has no tongue. He lives with Islav now, as his assistant.

I know a little about being found in the jungle by strangers.

That night we put down some skeletons. Later we saw a campfire on the bank, and rode past it.

PARLAS BADE US BRING ISLAV INGREDIENTS. WE BROUGHT NONE. HE GAVE US A POTION ALL THE SAME.

22 Tarsakh · eleven in the morning

Flaming Fist soldiers, coming towards us. They wanted to see our Charter of Exploration. (Fifty gold, at Fort Beluarian, which we never went to.) We rode straight through and provoked them a bit.

Their cleric paralysed Ofar, but the spell slid off me, so I provoked them further and in the end mooned them. I'm too short for that sort of thing, so Luth held me up, and I got a crossbow bolt in the backside, which I sort of deserved.

THEIR CLERIC HELD ME FAST. I COULD NOT MOVE. OLLI I COULD STILL SEE.

They were far too slow to catch us.

22 Tarsakh · evening

At eight we saw it: Firefinger, twenty kilometres off. A finger of rock standing straight up out of the jungle, with pterafolk circling the top.

Somewhere near it is the mine where Zhanthi's miners found me.

It was dark when we got there, and there was noise coming from the mine. Scarlett knelt by the river and Ofar hid her, which is no small thing to do with a triceratops who has a house on her back.

I HID SCARLETT: A TRICERATOPS WITH A HOUSE UPON HER BACK. I DID WHAT COULD BE DONE.

The miners spoke Chultan and wanted to know who we were. The foreman is called Carlos. And there's an old dwarf called Otto, who has supposedly worked here for twenty years. We went down into the mine to find him.

Otto looked at me for a long time before he told it.

Twenty years ago a wounded owlin brought a baby down from Firefinger, to keep it safe.

The baby was me.

OLLI HAS A PAST NOW. I AM GLAD FOR HIM. MINE HOLDS ELEVEN DEATHS.

The pterafolk had attacked the owlins on Firefinger and destroyed all of them in a single night. Afterwards Zhanthi came for me.

A wounded owlin: I keep turning those words over, wondering who he was, and whether he made it.

A REUNION. I KEPT THE WATCH.

I told Otto about the family who raised me: dead at the wedding, and held frozen by a spell until the curse is broken and they can be brought back.

THE SAME CURSE AS MINE. THEN WE BREAK IT, FOR US BOTH.

The miners hate the Zhentarim, and they hate the pterafolk. They're afraid every time they load the carts. Carlos offered us a good reward to clear Firefinger.

I'd have done it for free.

A mage tried to climb Firefinger a few months ago and never came back. At the foot of the rock we found bodies, and one of them was his.

Loot'ayen looted him. He was a wizard from Waterdeep, and according to his journal the pterafolk are clever enough to talk to.

1 spyglass · 2 healing potions ✓ · 10 insect repellent · 15 water tablets · a sending stone · journal · spellbook. — L.

22 Tarsakh · night · Firefinger

In the dead man's things, two words were written down like a password. We don't know yet what they open:

Schlingelidingdong. Öffnedi-pöffnedi.

ÖFFNEDI-PÖFFNEDI. SCHLINGELIDINGDONG.

Then up. I went first, fell off twice, broke the ladder, and got to the first level anyway. On the first level: a skeleton (definitely an orc), and a pit. Ofar fell into the pit, and the pit was full of spiders.

ON THE WAY UP I FELL INTO A PIT OF SPIDERS. A PRAYER OF HEALING, AND WE WENT ON.

Above the spider cave, a shaft went straight up, twenty-seven metres. All three of us tried to throw the rope up, and all three of us missed.

So we simply climbed it, which was dead easy.

Second level: bat-like things, and a dead man. In his purse, two little onyx statues of chwinga.

Third level: statues and steps, round the outside, up a ladder, and then a room with four pterafolk in it. We killed all four.

THE DEAD WIZARD'S BOOK SAYS PTERAFOLK CAN SPEAK. THESE DID NOT.

And in the corner of that room they had a prisoner.

An owlin. A real one: young, with his wings and his beak tied shut. His name is Nephyr.

It's the first time in my life I have seen another owlin. A few hours ago Otto told me they all died in one night.

Nephyr told us about Kersabal. Kir Sabal. An owlin village in the mountains by the River Olung. Six to nine days from here, probably.

6–9 DAYS. MY CURSE: 1–2 MONTHS. IT WILL SUFFICE. BARELY.

Then a fifth pterafolk came in, and found us waiting for it.

11–14 pterafolk. Now 6–5. — L.

On the Heart of Ubtao I wrote: Other owlins in Chult???

I can take the question marks off now.

22 Tarsakh · half past eleven at night · Firefinger

Still on the third level. The flat stone with the rune, from the dead wizard's bag, is a sending stone. So we tried it.

Somebody answered: Leomund Whitestone, a professor at the academy in Waterdeep. We told him his wizard was dead, down at the foot of Firefinger. He gave us his name and asked who we were.

It's a strange thing, telling a stranger far away that someone is dead. You only get a few words. None of them are the right ones.

Next room: bones in piles, and very old paintings on the walls. Three of them.

  • warriors from Omu fighting pterodactyls;
  • a warrior giving a guardian a crown made of leaves and vines;
  • the warrior lighting a fire on top of Firefinger.

The warrior is a paladin, and he carries a glaive.

A PALADIN DROVE OFF THE PTERODACTYLS AND LIT A FIRE. EVER SINCE, THEY FEAR FIRE. ANOTHER TOWER OF UBTAO, LIKE THE OTHER RUIN.

Then up the last shaft. I climbed it gloriously. Then we made a great deal of noise inside it, which told every pterafolk on the top that we were coming.

There were five of them, and their king, and it was close.

IT WAS CLOSE. ONCE I SAVED THEM BOTH. MOST OF THE FOE I SLEW.

Afterwards we took everything. In the pile: Azaka's tiger mask.

Azaka was going to guide us here to get it back from the pterafolk. Now we have the mask, and Azaka is in Port Nyanzaru, being afraid of us.

Tiger-head mask from the tower, big fangs. A very faint enchantment aura. — L.

On the way down, Nephyr told me something. I'm going to write it down twice.

The elder of his village can bring my wings back.

The elder of his village can bring my wings back.

With a ritual, he says. A bloody one. I'll think about the blood later.

The rest of the way down:

  • Luth knocked stones loose onto Ofar. Twice.
  • Ofar had words with him about it. Once.
  • I crashed down the shaft.
STONES UPON MY HEAD. TWICE. AT THE NEXT CLIFF, I CLIMB FIRST.

For the rest of the way down we used the feather fall scroll, and I still managed to get caught on a branch, and then to fall off it.

I hate climbing.

At the bottom lay the king of the pterafolk, dead. We took his crown. Then back to the mine, to sleep.

I think it's the crown from the second wall painting. I'd have to see the painting again to be sure, and I am not climbing up there again.

23 Tarsakh · at the mine

We woke up and realised we had left the pterafolk heads behind, our only proof. We forgot the proof.

Nephyr went back for them.

Nephyr and I collected the reward. Then the Flaming Fist turned up, looking for us. I hid, they saw me anyway the moment I ran, and they hit me once before Nephyr and I got away.

LUTH AND I WENT "FISHING". SAY NO MORE.

Then, finally, we unpacked the package from Ifan's office: the heavy one in oilcloth that had been riding in the howdah ever since, smelling of sulphur, while everybody found a reason not to open it.

SULPHIRA.

Two barrels, one above the other. Gold filigree like vines all the way along. Amber stones in the lock. A dark wooden grip that fits my hand as if somebody had measured it. Her name is Sulphira, and I may be in love.

23 Tarsakh · riding east

On the way to the Olung, Ofar attuned himself to the crown. For a moment he wasn't with us. He saw something, and he has written it in my margin in his own words, because I would get it wrong.

THE CROWN SHOWS ME A PALADIN FIGHTING YUAN-TI IN A CITY RINGED BY CLIFFS. NO MIST. THAT CITY I SHALL FIND.

And now he can go blurry. Only for a moment, and only when he wants to. It's very unsettling to look at.

Then cockatrices attacked us. A cockatrice is what you get when a chicken and a bat have a very bad idea together.

Fortunately for everyone, it was a short fight.

A COCKATRICE. IT LOOKS LIKE SUPPER. IT IS NOT. IT TURNS A MAN TO STONE.

At night we rode into a field of mushrooms, the kind you see things from, and Luth saw something.

Vision: a priest, or an authority, of the snake-people. Exactly unlike the yuan-ti. An inner room, on a bare raised platform. — L.

Nephyr led us round the rest of the field. It's good to have somebody in the party who can look at things from above.

23 Tarsakh · later that night

Ofar and Luth found a piece of paper nailed to a tree. When they found a second one, they woke me.

To Luth and me it was blank, but blood was dripping from the back of it.

Ofar could read it: it was written in his own blood.

"She sees through the trees. She knows our names."

MY BLOOD. HER WORDS. SHE WOULD HAVE ME AFRAID. NOT THIS DAY.

When he touched it, it came apart, and what it came apart into was red ants.

I'm writing this in the howdah by a hooded lantern. There are still a few ants walking across this page. I'm not killing them, and I'm not touching them either.

What they carried, Luth drew. I didn't want to touch any of it long enough to draw it myself.

Luth has written a name in my margin, next to them.

PAINT UPON MY NOSE. I WORE IT ALL EVENING, IN RESPECT.

She needs the feather for a ritual. And then all of us get wings.

All of us.

She does not seem to be telling quite the truth, but close. The feather: probably not strictly necessary. A ritual with a lot of blood. — L.

I want to believe her. Luth has written what he thinks underneath. I'm leaving it there.

And then she told us to go and find someone called Talira.

Talira is my mother (apparently my name is Tuvien

28 Tarsakh · night · the balcony

OLLI HAS FOUND HIS MOTHER. MINE IS AT HOME: LISTAZIA. I OUGHT TO SEND HER WORD.

Up here a gun is called a machine of death, and I don't know whether to be proud of that. A little, maybe.

It's a clear night. The jungle is completely black below us, and the stars go all the way down to it.

Thuvien. Thalira.

I've written them both wrong once already. I'm going to practise.

29 Tarsakh · Kir Sabal

THE PRINCESS IS PROUD. THE PRINCE PLAYS. I TRUST HIM WHO PLAYS.

We talked with Nephyr for a while and then slept, or in Luth's case meditated, and in the morning Luth said that Asharra isn't quite right.

Breakfast with Prince Na. He is a small human boy who dresses up as an owlin, and he is very playful. He showed us a book in a language like Chultan, but with slightly different letters.

A human, raised by owlins, dressed up as one.

I'm an owlin, raised by humans, dressed up as one of them. I laughed first, and then for a while I didn't laugh at all.

At the end of breakfast Princess Mwaxanaré came in. She wants us to bring back the Skull Chalice of Ch'gakare from Omu: a golden cup with a skull on it.

The legendary paladin is called Na N'buzo. I'd bet my last bullet he's the paladin with the glaive on the walls of Firefinger.

CH'GAKARE STRUCK OFF A HEAD AND WALKED OUT OF HELL. A CUP FOR SUCH A MAN. WE SHALL BRING IT.

After breakfast the owlins gave us firewood and three boards, and we left.

THREE BOARDS. WE TAKE THEM ALL.

One night: that is all I had with my mother.

The chalice is in Omu. The feather is in Omu, or in Nangalore. My brother is in Omu. So is whatever is killing everybody. It's all the same direction.

In the afternoon we reached the river and went on with Water Walk. At night, on the bank:

A triceratops, with a Red Wizard on its horn.

Luth fetched the body and the dead man's bag. He was a Red Wizard of Thay, a new one, and according to his journal he was on his way to Nangalore. Looking for a black orchid.

So are we.

One scroll of necromancy: destroyed. — L.
UNKNOWN POTIONS. WE TRY THEM FIRST ON SCARLETT. SHE IS THE LARGEST OF US.

30 Tarsakh

Xandala again, on the river. She wants us to travel with her. While we talked, Luth read her thoughts, and she read his at the very same time.

I just stood between them and looked from one to the other.

XANDALA TWISTS MINDS AGAIN. I NEED NO DETECT THOUGHTS TO SEE IT.

Nangalore · two in the morning

An arm of the river runs straight to the temple of Nangalore. We went in fast, with a light, up the canal in the middle, on Scarlett.

I called out, in my best Chultan:

"We come in peace."

OLLI'S CHULTAN IS NOT POOR. THE ANSWER WAS A NOISE IN THE DARK.

On the wall, four faces of the same woman, carved in stone, each in a different mood. Over each face a line of writing in Lower Chultan. We read them with the Red Wizard's scroll of Comprehend Languages.

By the canal there was a stone elephant. It had something to say too.

Elephant: Oh great Ubtao, free me. — L.

Three of the lines were praise. The fourth, over the face looking down her nose, said she was revered by Tirutaya, who loves betrayed her.

"Betrayed" was cut in later, over "loves". Weather doesn't do that; somebody did it with a chisel.

We left Scarlett and went on, and found the orchid with a spell.

It was in the room with Zalkoré.

Zalkoré talks to the air. — L.

We gave her five hundred gold in gems, and she gave us a black orchid.

We did not insult her. Ofar, I checked.

Then she wanted us to stay for dinner. Saying no would have been rude.

We looked at each other, and then we looked at the door.

We ran. Without a fight!!!

THE ORCHID IN HAND. NO FIGHT. LUTH PORTS, WE FLEE. A RETREAT WITH THE PRIZE IS A VICTORY.

We crossed the marsh so as not to run into Xandala again, and rode on towards Omu.

The priests of Savras said people who go to Nangalore don't come back, but we came back, all of us, and I didn't fire a single shot.

We are getting better at this.

−8 insect repellent. — L.

Greengrass

At home, Greengrass means flowers on every windowsill and far too much cake. This year my family is waiting under a spell, and I am in a bog.

The bog got thinner today, and the jungle started again.

Luth sent Nephyr, the young owlin from Firefinger who led us to Kir Sabal, a message to ask the way. A sending allows twenty-five words. Ours was supposed to end with "for now we're not coming back". It ended with:

The "not" fell off the end.

NEPHYR'S ROAD TO OMU: SOUTH OF THE LAKE, THEN WEST ACROSS THE STEPPES, PAST THE VOLCANO.

Then fat wasps attacked us. Their nest hung in a tree like a paper barrel. We won, and the nest was full of larvae.

It was a feast day, so we had a feast.

LARVAE. CRISP, THEN SOFT. A GOOD FEAST.

Ofar ate his like sausages, while Luth looked at his for a long time; I'm an owlin, so I had his as well.

After that, swamp again: very dense, all reeds, and thorn bushes that go straight through feathers.

In the evening Luth sent a second message, to Zhanthi in Port Nyanzaru, Father's old friend.

Hello Zhanthi, on our way to Omu, we are well. Do you have hints for Omu or the way there? We Luth and Ofar. — L.

I counted it afterwards. Twenty-three words. There were two to spare, and "and Olli" is two words.

Her answer: the yuan-ti are in Omu. She doesn't know the way. (And apparently we left a mess in Port Nyanzaru. That part I believe.)

THE CHAOS IN PORT NYANZARU WAS OUR DOING. IT WAS WORTH IT. ‖ ASHARRA IS NOT PLEASED. I DO NOT SERVE ASHARRA.

1 Mirtul

We reached an enormous lake.

GRUNGS HUNT GIANT DRAGONFLIES. ALFONS TAUGHT ME: SHOW THEM NO WEAKNESS.

  • zinc ingots
  • a smelting furnace

MY SHIELD. OLLI MADE IT. IT SHALL GO HOME TO THE TRIBE WITH ME.

He hasn't put it down since.

The earth shook twice while we worked, and once more in the night. Every time, dust comes down out of the rafters and onto this page. I've stopped blowing it off.

THE GROUND SHAKES, THE LAKE ANSWERS. CHULT WANTS US NOT. NO MATTER.

Out on the lake the waves are bigger than a lake's waves should be.

2 Mirtul

We went west, and the earth shook again, harder. Rain, black ground, and you can hardly see Scarlett's horns from the howdah.

  • peel
  • boil for eight hours
  • mash
  • eat

Seven portions. It keeps you going.

3 Mirtul

Fire newts and salamanders attacked us.

Otherwise nothing happened all day.

Ofar remembers 3 Mirtul differently. He painted it.

BY NIGHT THE VOLCANO ERUPTS. WE MAKE FOR THE FISSURE TO TELEPORT ACROSS. THINGS CRAWL OUT OF IT. ONE SEIZES ME. I NEARLY DIE. I DO NOT. WE CROSS.

In my defence, I was writing about the day.

Luth prayed us all back together, and we rode the whole day after.

4 Mirtul

We travelled all day.

4 MIRTUL: A DAY IN THE SADDLE. NAUGHT TO STRIKE.

5 Mirtul

We're back in the jungle.

In the evening we heard someone calling for help.

MONKS STRANGLED BY A VINE. I ATTACK THE VINE, AS ONE MUST.

????????

Two days of rain got into my bag. These pages were wet for a week. Whatever I wrote on them is gone, if I wrote anything at all.

Ofar says he wrote everything down. Ofar, these pages are yours.

UNDEAD, AND THE VINE. A MAN DIES AND A GHOST RISES FROM HIM. WE FIGHT, TAKE ONE BODY, LEAVE THE GHOST, AND RIDE ON. THEN A LONG REST.

6 MIRTUL. RAIN, MORE UNDEAD, A STORM FROM 16:00. A DEEP GORGE. WE PLAN THE CROSSING, AND FIGHT OUR WAY OVER ALL THE SAME.

NIGHT, AND RAIN. THE CURSE TAKES YET ANOTHER PIECE OF ME.

7 MIRTUL, ON THE LOOKOUT. FROM 25 METRES UP, WITH LUTH: A CLEARING 20 KM SOUTH-SOUTH-EAST. THERE LIES OUR WAY.

8 Mirtul · morning · the rim

Ofar has given the book back, and it is my turn again.

Omu.

Somewhere down there is the Soulmonger, the thing that holds on to the souls of the dead: Ofar's curse, my family's spell. And somewhere down there is a brother I have never met.

OMU. THE SOULMONGER LIES BELOW. HERE MY CURSE ENDS, ONE WAY OR THE OTHER.

What we could see from up here, through Luth's spyglass:

THE RED WIZARDS HAVE WALLED THEMSELVES IN. A "GATED COMMUNITY". I MARK IT UPON THE MAP.

Next: Wongo's shrine. Over the door: "Better to be Wongo's friend than his enemy."

Inside, a scowling stone monkey standing on its tail, and on the wall a monkey tearing a snake apart. Wongo and Moa, the snake, were enemies.

A MONKEY WHO HATES SNAKES. AT LAST, A GOD ON OUR SIDE.

A riddle with masks. We solved it, then fought the monkeys anyway, because the answer meant cursing our friends. Their bites make you berserk. Third cube.

Also, there was a book in there.

A very interesting book. Old, heavy, a skull on the cover. I don't remember much after I picked it up. Ofar says they had to tear it out of my hands and put it in a corner, and then I was normal again.

WE LAID THE BOOK IN THE CORNER, FACE DOWN. OLLI MARKED WHICH CORNER. I SAW HIM MARK IT.

I am normal.

It's still in that corner. I know exactly which corner.

We needed a rest, so we looked for a quiet house in an alley. We found an overgrown one. There was a vine in it.

The thing was fucking strong.

NEARLY ALL OF US DEAD. VINES AGAIN, TWICE IN THREE DAYS. HENCEFORTH I HATE VINES.

We ran, and one house further on we're resting now. I'm writing this soaked, by a shaded lantern.

Through the broken roof I can see the obelisk: black, and very tall. The letter said it's the door to the tomb. Orvex is asleep. Vaeril is at the window. Luth is meditating, and Ofar is pretending not to be tired.

evening · by the water

Luth cast a ritual so we could walk on water, and we walked across the flooded part of the city to the next shrine. Cranes carved everywhere: eblis. The god here is Papazotl. Over the door:

"Papazotl teaches us to bow before no one."

We didn't use the door. Luth shaped the stone of the back wall into a new one, and we walked in through that.

PAPAZOTL: A SLY GOD. WE GO IN THROUGH THE BACK WALL. SLYER STILL.

On one wall, a painting of crane-people and a poem about them: how they came down from the heights, and how they were the first, the true ones. One line stuck:

"The others still linger in the rocks and call themselves pure."

"The others in the rocks": cliffs, Kir Sabal. They mean us.

Inside: six statues of naked people with animal heads, and an empty pedestal with one more riddle.

We covered the statues' eyes, and the cube rose out of the pedestal, our fourth. Then a door opened, very slowly.

Two eblis.

8 Mirtul · night · Papazotl

The eblis smashed the door open, and the fight began.

TALL. THEY LOOK DOWN UPON ALL. NOT UPON ME.

They are tall, all legs and beak, and they look down at you the way a heron looks at a frog. Remember the poem. They were the first. They are the true ones.

We killed the first. The second tried to turn invisible and get away, and we threw everything we had after it; Ofar's glaive got stuck.

And I fired Sulphira.

Her first shot.

She jumped clean out of my hand, and what came out of the barrels was a beam of turquoise light, straight as a ruler.

The second eblis didn't get away.

I picked Sulphira up out of the water and held her for a while. Nobody said anything about it. Thank you, nobody.

We heard more movement inside the shrine, so we ran: north across the water, then west, back to the safehouse.

We rested, and I swapped my watch with somebody.

OLLI WISHED TO TRADE WATCHES. I SHOULD HAVE ASKED WHY.

Then I sneaked out.

Necromancy all-nighter.

The book was still in its corner. I told you I knew exactly which corner.

I found a roofless house where nobody would see the light, and I sat down with it, and I read it. All of it. All night.

I'm not going to write down what's in it. That isn't a lie. It's a decision.

I wasn't alone in there, though nobody with me was alive.

Meanwhile, back at the house, a Red Wizard tried to sneak in, invisible. Vaeril took him completely apart.

I missed it, being busy elsewhere.

THE DEAD WIZARD'S AMULET AND SENDING STONE: VAERIL HIDES THEM IN HIS CLOAK. I SAW IT. I WRITE IT DOWN.

Two green potions from him. They smell like a tannery on fire, and apparently they're good for you.

9 Mirtul · morning

I came back, got called to account, and told them everything.

Everything, in about the first five seconds. You know me by now.

I am disappointed. — L.
OLLI READ THE BOOK ALL NIGHT. NEXT TIME I SHALL TAKE HIS WATCH MYSELF.

Then Luth told Vaeril that he is the only trustworthy one among us.

Vaeril has known us for one day. I've told everybody everything, every single time. I'm just saying.

We set off along the top of the cliff, then walked on the water along the foot of it. Two new obelisks, and stone frogs: grungs. The shrine of Nangnang.

Nangnang was vain and afraid of everything. He was hunted by Shagambi, a leopard with snakes' heads at its sides, because he stole the spear Shagambi meant to drive the evil out of Omu with.

A COWARD STEALS THE SPEAR THAT MIGHT SAVE THE CITY. I BEAR A GLAIVE. I DO NOT RUN.

Luth cast a spell to find the owlins' necklace. Twenty or thirty metres under the ground, right in the middle. Under the palace.

BENEATH THE PALACE, WHERE VAERIL'S FRIENDS ARE HELD. GOOD: ONE ROAD FOR BOTH TASKS.

We climbed over the palace wall. Orvex stayed behind.

Then a voice spoke to Luth, out of nowhere: "Cooperation could be useful." It led us into a house and up some stairs. A Red Wizard was waiting there, a woman.

One half of her face was young, the other very old.

I couldn't stop looking at the line where they meet.

She wants us to work together. They have some of the cubes, we have some, and Ras Nsi has one. They want to destroy the soulmonger too, she says.

HALF A GIRL OF 18, HALF A CRONE. BOTH HALVES LIE.

We don't trust her, of course.

We're making a plan.

book.title: Oliver's Chult Journal
card: Sessions 31 to 48: Omu, the Fane of the Night Serpent and the Tomb of the Nine Gods.

defaults.credit: Drawn by Oliver · ink and wash

variants.title: Albino dwarf · Jungle guide
variants.text: Their guide: an albino dwarf in armour of dinosaur bone, with a wooden maul. Knows the way, mostly, and dreams of a mine of his own.

variants.title: Half-orc · Cleric of Torm (Order of the Gauntlet)
variants.text: A half-orc cleric of Torm who shared the ship to Chult and walked into the jungle with them; later she escorted the wounded down from Camp Vengeance.

variants.title: Owlin · Gunslinger (Fighter / Rogue)
variants.text: The writer of this journal. An owlin raised by a human merchant family in Baldur's Gate; a tinkerer who loves his guns and cannot tell a lie to save his life. He came to Chult because his family can't be brought back while the death curse holds.

variants.title: Owlin · Gunslinger and necromancer (Fighter / Rogue / Wizard)
variants.text: Since one sleepless night in Omu with a skull-bound book, he raises the dead about as well as he shoots. Still a terrible liar, so everyone knows.

variants.name: Oliver Lyonbrooke · Thuvien
variants.title: Owlin · Gunslinger and necromancer
variants.text: His wings are back, given by a Wind Duke because his brother asked. Born Thuvien in Kir Sabal, raised Oliver in Baldur's Gate: both.

variants.title: Elf · Cleric of the Raven Queen
variants.text: The dead no longer reach the Raven Queen. Somewhere in the south their souls are caught, and her halls stand silent. She has sent me to find what holds them, and to break it. A raven flies ahead of me. Where it goes, I follow; where it lands, I kneel. My born name I leave unwritten. Shar's priests know it, and hunt it. Let them. All that I am is hers: my breath, my name, my years. She need only ask. — L.

variants.title: Elf · Soul Warden of the Raven Queen
variants.text: Found among my drawings. My hand drew it. I do not know who he was. Below it, in the same hand: the souls are free. I am to lead them home.

variants.title: Triceratops · Ofar's steed
variants.text: Ofar's summoned steed: his paladin's Find Steed, which since the witch's dream comes as a young triceratops. Pulls boats when the water holds her, carries a howdah, and walks through fences.

variants.title: Giant lizard · Ofar's summon
variants.text: Ofar's summoned giant lizard: climbs walls, carries riders, goes hunting at night. Oliver calls him Coco Jambo.

variants.title: Dwarf · Lieutenant of the Order of the Gauntlet
variants.text: A dwarf with a beard like a bonfire who took them upriver with his soldiers and later held Camp Vengeance together. Ofar started his fan chant.

variants.title: Human (Chultan) · Paladin, Oath of Vengeance
variants.text: I CROSSED THE SEA TO END THE CURSE: TO RAISE MY KIN AND MY FRIENDS FROM THE DEAD, AND TO STAY MINE OWN DEATH. ELEVEN TEETH UPON MY SKIN: ELEVEN TIMES HAVE I DIED, ELEVEN TIMES RETURNED. A HAG'S CURSE RUNS IN MY BLOOD. BY NIGHT, THE RED ANTS. BY MORNING, BLOOD FROM MY NOSE. MY VILLAGE LIES IN THE JUNGLE, TWO DAYS FROM BALDUR'S GATE. MINE OWN CARDS I PAINT. NO OTHER HAND GETS MY FACE RIGHT.
variants.credit: Painted by Ofar himself · gouache on a loose card

variants.title: Human (Chultan) · Paladin, Oath of Vengeance
variants.text: THE GLAIVE OF THE FALLEN KING. AMONG THE DEAD, NA'NBUZO PUT ME TO THE TEST. I HELD FAST TILL HIS LIGHT BURNED IN ME, AND I DREW THE BLADE FROM THE STONE. RED RIBBONS. AN EDGE LIKE A LIVE COAL. A CRY LIKE A WAR HORN. A KING BORE IT ONCE. NOW I BEAR IT, UNTO THE END.
variants.credit: Painted by Ofar himself · gouache on a loose card

variants.title: Human (Chultan) · Paladin, Oath of Vengeance
variants.text: THE PLATE OF A KNIGHT OF THE YELLOW BANNER. HE DIED DOWN HERE, STILL CLAD IN IT. BY PRAYER I FOUND HIM, AND FROM HIS BONES I TOOK IT. HE DID NOT COME OUT. I SHALL. NOW AT LAST I LOOK WHAT I HAVE ALWAYS SAID I WAS.
variants.credit: Painted by Ofar himself · gouache on a loose card

variants.title: Human · Former scribe of the Red Wizards
variants.text: A balding scribe who walked away from the Red Wizards and reads Old Omuan. He knows the tomb better than anyone should, and he tells everyone their stories.

variants.name: Vaeril
variants.title: Owlin · Scout from Kir Sabal (so he says)
variants.text: An owlin from Kir Sabal with a green hood, a sword, and a pair of wings that make Oliver jealous. He knocked on a shrine door in Omu and says his friends are prisoners in the palace.

variants.title: Owlin · Warlock, pact of the blade (patron: a Wind Duke of Aaqa)
variants.text: He was never Vaeril. Tarkil of Kir Sabal, warlock of a Wind Duke, and maybe Oliver's brother. He lectures Oliver about honesty.

variants.title: Owlin · Warlock, pact of the blade (patron: a Wind Duke of Aaqa)
variants.text: Tarkil of Kir Sabal, warlock of a Wind Duke, and Oliver's brother: a question asked out loud in Omu said yes. Same height, same feathers.

variants.title: Owlin · Guide from Kir Sabal
variants.text: A young owlin they cut loose in a cave by the river. He showed them the way to Kir Sabal, and for a while he was not quite himself.
